theory.intro: The word **rate** says how quickly a quantity is changing, and this language works for any quantity: a population, a temperature, a water level. A straight line changes at a constant rate; a curve’s rate is itself changing.
facts: The description refers to how the **steepness** changes, not to the size of the quantity itself.
steps: Decide whether the quantity is increasing, decreasing, or staying constant.
Decide whether the graph is straight (a constant rate) or curved.
If it is curved, decide whether it is getting steeper (an increasing rate) or flatter (a decreasing rate).
Combine the two decisions into the full phrase, e.g. 'increasing at a decreasing rate'.

workedExamples.solution_text:
Read each graph from left to right. First identify whether $Q$ rises or falls, then check whether the steepness stays constant, increases or decreases.

A: $Q$ increases at a constant rate. The rising line has constant steepness.

B: $Q$ increases at an increasing rate. The rising curve gets steeper.

C: $Q$ increases at a decreasing rate. The rising curve gets flatter.

D: $Q$ decreases at a constant rate. The falling line has constant steepness.

E: $Q$ decreases at an increasing rate. The falling curve gets steeper.

F: $Q$ decreases at a decreasing rate. The falling curve gets flatter.

Cyclist P's graph rises and gets steeper. Distance from home increases at an increasing rate, so P speeds up.

Cyclist R's graph rises and gets flatter. Distance from home increases at a decreasing rate, so R slows down.

The cyclists reach the same final distance, but their changing steepness shows different speed patterns.

a. Graph N: it rises and gets flatter, so the money collected increases at a decreasing rate.

b. Graph M: it is a rising straight line, so the money collected increases at a constant rate.

c. Graph L: it rises and gets steeper, so the money collected increases at an increasing rate.

A: the horizontal line shows a constant number of cups available; the rate of change is zero.

B: the falling straight line shows the number decreasing at a constant rate.

C: the falling curve gets steeper, so the number decreases at an increasing rate.

Between C and D, the upward jump could represent a batch of clean cups being added at once.

D: the falling curve gets flatter, so the number decreases at a decreasing rate.

foundation.solution_text:
The graph rises, so the population is increasing.
The curve gets steeper as time passes, so the population is increasing at an increasing rate.

The graph rises, so the crowd size is increasing.
The curve gets flatter as time passes, so the crowd size is increasing at a decreasing rate.

The graph falls, so the charge is decreasing.
The curve gets steeper as time passes, so the charge is decreasing at an increasing rate.

The graph falls, so the temperature is decreasing.
The curve gets flatter as time passes, so the temperature is decreasing at a decreasing rate.
The graph is a straight line, not a curve, so the fare is increasing at a constant rate — the steepness never changes.

The graph rises, so the temperature is increasing.
The curve gets flatter as time passes, so the temperature is increasing at a decreasing rate.

development.solution_text:
Country X's curve gets steeper over time, so its population is increasing at an increasing rate — its growth is speeding up.
Country Y's curve gets flatter over time, so its population is increasing at a decreasing rate — its growth is levelling off.

Stage 1 (heating): the curve rises but gets flatter, so the temperature is increasing at a decreasing rate as it approaches the furnace's maximum.
Stage 2 (held at maximum): the line is flat, so the temperature stays constant.
Stage 3 (cooling): the curve falls and gets flatter, so the temperature is decreasing at a decreasing rate as it cools.

Graph Q shows revenue increasing at an increasing rate.
Graph P is a straight line, so it shows a constant rate, and Graph R gets flatter over time, so it shows a decreasing rate. Only Graph Q gets steeper over time, matching an increasing rate.

The graph falls and gets steeper as time passes, so the number of unsold tickets is decreasing at an increasing rate.
The increasing steepness shows that tickets are being sold more quickly, so sales are speeding up.

Battery X's curve gets steeper over time, so its charge is decreasing at an increasing rate — it is losing charge faster and faster.
Battery Y's curve gets flatter over time, so its charge is decreasing at a decreasing rate — it is losing charge more and more slowly.

Stage 1 (tap running): the line is straight, so the water height is increasing at a constant rate.
Stage 2 (tap off and plug in place): the line is flat, so the water height stays constant.
Stage 3 (draining): the curve falls and gets flatter, so the water height is decreasing at a decreasing rate.

mastery.solution_text:
Stage 1 (before school): the line is flat, so the number of cans stays constant — no one is buying.
Stage 2 (morning break): the line is straight and falling, so the number of cans decreases at a constant rate.
Stage 3 (lunchtime rush): the curve falls and gets steeper, so the number of cans decreases at an increasing rate as sales speed up.
Stage 4 (restock): the number of cans jumps straight up, showing an instant change.
Stage 5 (afternoon): the curve falls but gets flatter, so the number of cans decreases at a decreasing rate as sales taper off.

Country A's curve gets steeper over time, so its population is increasing at an increasing rate.
Country B's curve gets flatter over time, so its population is increasing at a decreasing rate.

The graph falls, so the water level is decreasing.
The curve gets steeper as time passes, so the water level is decreasing at an increasing rate — it is falling more quickly as time passes.
